name: Kaamba
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog cites only Bantu classification papers (Pacchiarotti et al. 2019, Bostoen & de Schryver 2018)

sources.citation: Patin, Cédric. 2013. De l'importance des langues bantu pour l'analyse des phénomènes d'interface. Histoire Épistémologie Langage 35(1): 83-108.
sources.note: Persée full-text search matches 'Kaamba' in this prosody-syntax interface paper; if it cites Kaamba prosodic data (presumably via Bouka 1989) it would be the only secondary statement on Kaamba prosody. PDF is altcha-gated.

sources.citation: Bouka, Léonce Yembi. 1994. L'accord des adjectifs du protobantou en zone H. Africana Linguistica 11: 13-18.
sources.note: Same author as the Kaamba thesis; adjective agreement in zone H, front matter only retrievable; not about prosody.

sources.citation: Laman, Karl Edvard. 1936. Dictionnaire kikongo-français avec une étude phonétique décrivant les dialectes les plus importants de la langue dite kikongo. Bruxelles: Institut Royal Colonial Belge.
sources.note: Introduction §20 (general Kongo, not Kaamba): 'En Kongo, les mots ont, dans la règle, l'accent principal (étymologique) sur la syllabe radicale et un accent secondaire (rythmique) assez fort sur la pénultième.' Its dialect list (Bembe, Mayombe, Kunyi=NO, Ndingi, Kakongo, Vili, N/S/E/O etc.) does not include Kamba/Kaamba, so this cannot be read as a Kaamba statement.

sources.citation: Laman, Karl Edvard. 1922. The musical accent or intonation in the Kongo language. Stockholm: Svenska Missionsförbundets förlag.
sources.note: §2: 'The root-accent always falls on the root-syllable.. The rhythmic accent is a secondary accent that always falls on the penult'; §28-29 strong stress movable by pitch. Dialects covered: Bembe, Kingoyi, Kinkenge, Madzia, Mayombe, Mazinga, Ndingi, Teke, Yaka — Kaamba not among them.

sources.citation: Goes, Heidi & Koen Bostoen. 2024. Vowel harmony and the morphophonology of the verb ending *-ide in the Kikongo Language Cluster (West-Coastal Bantu): a historical-comparative analysis. Studies in African Linguistics 53(1). doi:10.32473/sal.53.1and2.129676
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Kikamba example (74) 'Babokodi' cited from Bouka 1989; classifies Kikamba as North Kikongo with back pVHH; full bibliographic entry for Bouka 1989.

sources.citation: Goes, Heidi & Koen Bostoen. 2019. Progressive vowel height harmony in Proto-Kikongo and Proto-Bantu. Journal of African Languages and Linguistics 40(1). doi:10.1515/jall-2019-0003
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Gives Kikamba (H112A) verb data from Bouka 1989 (appendix ex. 23, tone-marked) and from KongoKing fieldwork by Guy Kouarata 2016 (ex. 24); notes Bouka's data are 'very limited and contradictory' for back vowel harmony (p. 37).
sources.venue: Journal of African Languages and Linguistics

sources.citation: de Schryver, Gilles-Maurice, Rebecca Grollemund, Simon Branford & Koen Bostoen. 2015. Introducing a state-of-the-art phylogenetic classification of the Kikongo Language Cluster. Africana Linguistica 21: 87-162.
sources.note: Classification paper; Persée full-text search matches 'Kaamba' (data-source list) but the PDF is altcha-protected and only the front matter was retrievable. No stress content expected.

sources.citation: Dom, Sebastian & Koen Bostoen. 2015. Examining variation in the expression of tense/aspect to classify the Kikongo Language Cluster. Africana Linguistica 21: 163-211.
sources.note: Tense/aspect classification; front matter only retrievable; no stress content.

sources.citation: Bouka, Léonce Yembi. 1989. Éléments de description du kaamba, parler bantou de la République Populaire du Congo (Groupe Koongo, H17b). Bruxelles: Université libre de Bruxelles, mémoire de licence. 262 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The only descriptive source for Kaamba (Glottolog ref 123680); 262 pp. with a tone-marked phonology (its data are reproduced with tone marks by Goes & Bostoen 2019, 2024), so any statement about accent/stress in Kaamba would be here.

sources.citation: Kouarata, Guy Noël. 2016. KongoKing fieldwork data on Kikamba (H112A), Ghent University KongoKing project (unpublished).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only recent first-hand Kaamba data (used in Goes & Bostoen 2019: ex. 24; 2024: ex. 48, 101); tone-marked; a KongoKing-derived sketch or wordlist could carry a note on accent. Kouarata has published Beembe grammar/dictionary with Edilivre (2015, 2016), so a Kikamba sketch may exist.

sources.citation: Mabiala, Jean-Noël. 1999. Phonologie comparative et historique du koongo. Lyon: Université Lumière Lyon 2, thèse de doctorat.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Comparative phonology of the Kongo varieties, cited by Goes & Bostoen 2019 for the KLC; likely to include Kaamba data and a suprasegmental section; not in theses.fr and the Lyon 2 repository was unreachable.

sources.citation: Lumwamu, François. 1974. Éléments pour un lexique kongo-français (dialectes dondo-kamba-kuni). Dimi: Revue du Centre pour l'Étude des Langues Congolaises 2: 20-87.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Earliest lexical material specifically covering the Kamba (Kaamba) dialect alongside Dondo and Kunyi; a Brazzaville CELCO publication that may carry a short phonological/prosodic introduction.
sources.venue: Dimi: Revue du Centre pour l'Étude des Langues Congolaises
